chunks: Muhammad ibn Ya'qub narrated from Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, or others, from Ibn Muskhan, from Abu Basir, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

I asked him about the Sunnah divorce. He said: The Sunnah divorce is when a man intends to divorce his wife; if he has consummated the marriage with her, he leaves her until she menstruates and then becomes pure. When she becomes pure, he divorces her once in the presence of two witnesses. Then he leaves her until she completes three menstrual periods. When three periods have passed, she is definitively divorced from him by one divorce, and her husband is suitor among the suitors; if she wishes, she can marry him, and if she wishes, she does not.

If she marries him with a new dowry, she is with him on two remaining divorces, and one has passed. If he divorces her once more while she is pure, in the presence of two witnesses, then leaves her until her periods pass, and when her periods pass before he revokes her, she is definitively divorced from him by two divorces, and she has control of her affairs and is permissible for other husbands, and her husband is a suitor among the suitors; if she wishes, she can marry him, and if she wishes, she does not.

If he marries her with a new marriage and a new dowry, she is with him on one remaining divorce, and two have passed. If he wishes to divorce her with a divorce that does not make her permissible to him until she marries another husband, he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he witnesses upon her divorce one divorce. Then she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.

As for the divorce of the waiting period, he leaves her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then he divorces her in the presence of two witnesses. Then he revokes her and consummates with her, then he waits with her for purity. When she menstruates and becomes pure, he has two witnesses witness upon another divorce. Then he revokes her and consummates with her, then he waits with her for purity. When she menstruates and becomes pure, he has the two witnesses witness upon the third divorce. Then she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband.

And upon her is to observe three menstrual periods from the day he divorces her with the third divorce. If he divorces her once while pure with witnesses, then waits with her until she menstruates and becomes pure, then divorces her before he revokes her, the second divorce is not a divorce because he divorced a divorcer, because when the woman is divorced from her husband, she is outside his ownership until he revokes her. When he revokes her, she returns to his ownership as long as he has not divorced the third divorce.

When he divorces her with the third divorce, the right of revocation leaves his hand. If he divorces her while pure with witnesses, then revokes her and waits with her for purity without consummation, she menstruates and becomes pure, then he divorces her before he defiles her with consummation after the revocation, his divorce of her is not a divorce because he divorced her the second divorce in the purity of the first. Therefore, the purity is not invalidated except by the consummation of the revocation.

And likewise, the third divorce does not occur except by revocation and consummation after the revocation, then menstruation and purity after the menstruation, then divorce with witnesses, so that for each divorce there is a period of purity from the defilement of consummation with witnesses.

Muhammad ibn al-Hasan said: What this report encompasses is that when he divorces her three divorces for the Sunnah, she is not permissible to him until she marries another husband, and this is the relied-upon view in my opinion and the one depended upon, because it agrees with the apparent meaning of the Book.

Allah the Exalted said: 'Divorce is twice. Then either keep [her] in an acceptable manner or release [her] with good treatment.' Until His saying: 'And if he divorces her [the third time], then she is not permissible to him afterwards until she marries a husband other than him.'
And He did not distinguish between the Sunnah divorce and the divorce of the waiting period, so the verse should be understood in its generality, and the report confirms it and indicates it as well.

key_terms.رَجْعَةٌ: Right of revocation (husband's right to take back wife during waiting period)
key_terms.طَلَاقُ السُّنَّةِ: Sunnah divorce (divorce given during the waiting period before consummation/revocation)
key_terms.طَلَاقُ الْعِدَّةِ: Divorce of the waiting period (revocation divorce)
key_terms.قُرُوءٌ: Menstrual periods (used to count the waiting period)

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Sunnah divorce and divorce of the waiting period in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Isfabar elucidates the precise mechanics of 'Talaq al-Sunnah' versus 'Talaq al-'Iddah', emphasizing that for a triple divorce to be binding and require 'Nikah al-Muhallil' (marriage to another man), each pronouncement must occur in a distinct period of purity following sexual consummation. Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that the third divorce severs the right of revocation, a ruling supported by Shaykh al-Tusi as the authoritative position because it aligns with the general principle of Quran 2:229. The text further details the specific conditions under which a divorce might be considered premature or invalid if not accompanied by the requisite waiting period and consummation.
